mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Scattered thunderstorm activity continues to develop east and south of the Lake Michigan vicinity, but the risk for additional severe weather appears to be lowering enough that a new severe weather watch is not anticipated.

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Lingering convection now generally spreading across and to the east/south of the southern Lake Michigan vicinity appears rooted within forcing for ascent associated with lower/mid-tropospheric warm advection. This is downstream of a low-amplitude short wave perturbation which is forecast to continue across the southwestern Great Lakes region overnight. A small clustering of storms now to the northwest of Danville IL appears the lone activity maintaining roots near the surface, within a boundary-layer characterized by seasonably high moisture content including dew points in the lower/mid 70s F. Located along a 30-35+ kt west-southwesterly 850 mb jet axis, near-surface hodographs are characterized by large clockwise curvature supportive of updraft rotation, though there is a weakness in flow further aloft, particularly with south/southeastward extent from the current position of the stronger convection. As activity continues to develop east-southeastward into a somewhat less moist air mass, any lingering risk for tornadoes seems likely to diminish. Potential for a couple of strong surface gusts may persist, but it is not clear that this will require a new severe weather watch.
